requirement:
No prompt, tool result, or tool error the harness gives the model MUST state a
line number or line range of a project source, except within source text it
quotes and where a tool error repeats a line number the model supplied. The
harness MUST identify a source location by file and outline selector under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors` instead.
rationale:
I found no gap against `requirements.authoring.no_line_numbers`. This is a static review of the code and tests.

The requirement has two parts: no prompt, tool result or tool error states a line number of a project source, and locations are identified by file and outline selector.

**Tool results**
- Line-range reads (the `habeas` line-range form) go through `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[read_lines]`, which returns inputs built by `read_selector`. `src/inputs.rs#impl[InputSelector]/fn[to_model_input]` and `to_input` give only file, item, hash, kind and text, never `line_start` or `line_end`.
- The `outline` tool's `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[outline_entries]` returns item, kind, name and children.
- The `ripgrep`, `ast_grep` and declared-query results share `src/authoring/tools.rs#impl[SearchNodes]/fn[entries]`. It emits file, selector, kind and `{text, matched}` lines, with an elision line between windows and no numbers.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[references]` returns name, role, file and item selector. Line numbers are used only to sort the sites.

**Prompts**
- Mandatory inputs reach the model through `model_mandatory_inputs`, which carries only selectors, hashes and text.
- Site prompts use `src/sites.rs#impl[SiteItem]/fn[matches_value]`, which gives kind, query, item selector and redacted text only.
- Citation prompts use `model_citations_value`, which gives role, name and commentary only.
- The `habeas` tool description says that results never give line numbers. Its `line_start`/`line_end` example is a request-format illustration, not a statement of a project source's location. I read it as outside the requirement.

**Tool errors**
- `read_lines` repeats only the numbers the model supplied, in `{file}:{requested} is not an inclusive range…`.
- Every tool error passes through `line_numbers::without_source_lines` in the `Err` arm of `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]`. It strips `line N: `, `at line N, column M`, `file:N: ` and `path:N` forms. It keeps the supplied range only when the text after it begins with ` is not an inclusive range`.
- When the model supplies a range such as `99-100`, the regex strips the first number and leaves `src/a.rs-100`. It does not leak an unsupplied line number, so I do not count it as a gap.

**Tests**
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]` and `fn[line_range_reads_record_the_innermost_covering_nodes]` assert that read results carry no `line_start` or `line_end`.
- `fn[search_merges_context_windows_and_respects_ignore_rules]` and `fn[separate_windows_in_one_node_are_divided_by_an_elision_line]` assert that search lines carry no line numbers.
- `fn[outline_lists_nested_nodes_without_text_or_inputs]` and `fn[references_list_names_and_flattened_sites_without_recording_inputs]` assert exact outline and reference results with no line numbers.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[tool_errors_give_the_model_no_line_numbers_it_did_not_supply]` covers the past-the-end range error repeating the supplied line, and covers a parse error, end to end through `assess`, reaching the model without its line.
- `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[tool_errors_drop_the_source_line_of_a_parse_error]` covers the parse-error, `file:N:`, "first declared at", YAML and TOML forms.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[site_reviews_use_their_prompt_and_record_applies_and_the_site]` checks the site subject message's matches (kind, query and item selector).
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs]` asserts the exact mandatory-input JSON.

Every obligation has a test that runs its code and asserts the outcome. The impl-marked code is either reachable from the {impl} items or itself carries the {impl} reference, and I found no unspecified behavior or {fixme} to account for.

text: No prompt, tool result, or tool error the harness gives the model MUST state a
line number or line range of a project source, except within source text it
quotes and where a tool error repeats a line number the model supplied. The
harness MUST identify a source location by file and outline selector under
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
